_README: Reverse-coverage allowlist for the FFI bridges, consumed by the test
`every_exported_ffi_fn_is_registered_or_allowlisted` in
crates/scp-testing/tests/integration/ffi_conformance.rs.
Every fn a bridge exports under its `src/` must be either (a) registered
as a parity operation in scripts/bridge-aliases.json, (b) listed here in
the bridge's array as a legitimately-non-parity export, or (c) listed in
pending_registration as a known-unregistered cross-bridge parity op
awaiting an alias entry.
Each entry has REQUIRED fields `name` and `path`, plus `kind` and `reason`.
`path` is the workspace-relative source file that defines the exported fn
(e.g. crates/scp-ffi/src/identity.rs). The gate matches on the QUALIFIED
key `<path>::<name>` — mirroring scripts/pure-helpers-allowlist.txt — so an
entry exempts ONLY the specific fn in the specific file it was written for.
A bare-name match would silently swallow any future op sharing the name
(e.g. a genuine op named `tools`, colliding with the `tools` getter),
recreating the hide-by-omission class this gate exists to kill. The same
fn name in two files needs two entries, one per path.
kind values: getter | lifecycle | dunder | wasm-only | test-fixture |
introspection | constructor | bridge-specific | pending-registration.
`bridge-specific` marks an export that is legitimately implemented in ONLY
one bridge by design (verified against .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json
or the bridge's binding model) — NOT a parity gap. Do not register these in
bridge-aliases.json: doing so would make the other bridges report 'missing'.
Its `reason` MUST reference the capability-matrix justification
(sdk-capability-matrix.json) OR an existing ADR-NNN / §N / SCP-NNN.
`wasm-only` and `pending-registration` reasons MUST cite a durable
artifact (ADR-NNN / §N / SCP-NNN), and every cited ADR/SCP token must
actually EXIST in the repo corpus (.docs/adrs, .docs/prds) — a fabricated
ADR-999 / SCP-9999 is rejected. The other kinds need a non-empty reason.
This file is an enforcement artifact: only ADD entries (or remove an entry
once the export it covers is deleted/registered). Weakening requires human
approval.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_claim_shadow
pyo3.reason: Claims a bridge shadow identity via identity attestation (ADR-023; spec §12.2.1). PyO3-only helper in bridge_connector.rs; the registered cross-bridge op is bridge_create_shadow, not claim. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_derive_credential_key
pyo3.reason: Derives a per-bridge credential encryption key (ADR-023; spec §12.11.2). PyO3-only crypto helper in bridge_connector.rs; the cross-bridge credential ops (bridge_credential_provision, bridge_credential_retrieve, bridge_credential_rotate, bridge_credential_revoke, bridge_credential_list, bridge_credential_store_key, bridge_credential_get_key, bridge_credential_delete_key) are registered separately. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_generate_credential_key
pyo3.reason: Generates a random bridge credential key (ADR-023; spec §12.11.2). PyO3-only crypto helper in bridge_connector.rs; the cross-bridge credential ops are registered separately. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_oauth_build_auth_url
pyo3.reason: Builds an OAuth 2.0 authorization URL for a bridge connector (ADR-023; spec §12.2.1). PyO3-only convenience helper in bridge_connector.rs; not among the 11 cross-bridge Bridge ops in .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_oauth_generate_pkce
pyo3.reason: PKCE S256 challenge generation for bridge-connector OAuth (ADR-023; spec §12.2.1). PyO3-only convenience helper in bridge_connector.rs; not among the 11 cross-bridge Bridge ops in .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_oauth_scopes_for_mode
pyo3.reason: Returns recommended OAuth scopes for a bridge mode (ADR-023; spec §12.2.1). PyO3-only convenience helper in bridge_connector.rs; not among the 11 cross-bridge Bridge ops in .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_open_shadow_envelope
pyo3.reason: Opens a sender-key-encrypted bridge shadow envelope (ADR-023; spec §12.10.2). PyO3-only crypto helper in bridge_connector.rs; not among the 11 cross-bridge Bridge ops in .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json. Not a parity gap.

pyo3.name: py_bridge_seal_shadow_envelope
pyo3.reason: Seals a sender-key-encrypted bridge shadow envelope (ADR-023; spec §12.10.2). PyO3-only crypto helper in bridge_connector.rs; not among the 11 cross-bridge Bridge ops in .docs/standards/sdk-capability-matrix.json. Not a parity gap.

Not a parity gap.

Not a cross-bridge parity op.

pending_registration._comment: Two UniFFI candidates remain pending registration: register_local_did and is_local_did (crates/scp-ffi/uniffi/src/bridge.rs). They are genuine cross-bridge candidates — UniFFI exposes them as Scp methods, while PyO3/NAPI only call core register_local_did/is_local_did internally and never export a free-fn form — so no bridge-aliases.json canonical exists yet. They stay here (treated as allowed, keeping the gate green) until a canonical alias entry lands. Seven earlier candidates (metadata_record_to_json, commit_deploy, rollback_deploy, transport_add_relay, transport_assign_relay_set, transport_adapter_count, transport_reliability) were REGISTERED in scripts/bridge-aliases.json; the remaining one-bridge exports were reclassified as `bridge-specific` in the per-bridge arrays above. A future genuine parity GAP — an op present in some-but-not-all applicable bridges that ought to be implemented everywhere — goes here with `kind:pending-registration` and durable provenance until the missing bridges land it.
